translations.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen people living as foreigners, scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

who were chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the sanctifying work of the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace increase among you.
Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy has given us new birth through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, into the hope of life
and into an inheritance that cannot decay, be defiled, or fade away, which is prepared for you in heaven,
while you are guarded by the power of God and through faith for the life that is ready to be revealed in the last times.
In those times you will rejoice forever, even though for a little while now you are distressed by the various trials that come upon you,
so that the proven quality of your faith may be seen—more precious than refined gold tested by fire—and result in praise, honor, and acclaim when Jesus Christ is revealed,
You love him whom you have not seen, and through faith in him you rejoice with glorious joy that cannot be expressed.
so that you may receive the reward of your faith: life for your souls.
The prophets investigated this life when they prophesied about the grace that was to be given to you.
They searched to discover what time the Spirit of Christ dwelling in them was indicating and testifying about, when Christ's sufferings would come and his glory afterward.

Everything they were investigating was revealed to them, because they were not seeking it for themselves, but were prophesying for us about things belonging to us. These things have now been revealed to you through those who brought you the good news by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look closely into these things.
Therefore, prepare your minds for action and be fully alert. Set your hope on the joy coming to you when our Lord Jesus Christ is revealed,
as obedient children. Do not become involved again in your former desires, the things you used to crave in ignorance.
Instead, be holy in all your conduct, just as the one who called you is holy.
For it is written, “Be holy, just as I also am holy.”
And if you call him Father, the one who shows no favoritism and judges everyone according to their deeds, conduct yourselves in reverent fear during this time of your stay as foreigners.
You know that you were redeemed from the empty practices you inherited from your ancestors, not with silver that perishes or with gold,
but with the precious blood of a lamb without defect or blemish, who is Christ.
He was set apart beforehand for this, before the foundations of the world, and was revealed at the end of the times for your sake.
Through him you have believed in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might rest on God.
Let your souls be holy through obedience to the truth, and let them be filled with love that shows no partiality, so that you love one another from a pure and perfect heart.
You are people who have been born anew, not from seed that perishes, but from seed that does not perish, through the living word of God, which endures forever.
For all flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the flower of the field. The grass dries up, and the flower withers,
but the word of our God stands forever. And this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.
Therefore put away from yourselves all wickedness, all deceit and favoritism, envy, and slander.
Be like newborn infants, and long for the word as for pure, spiritual milk, so that through it you may grow into life.
If you have tasted and seen that the Lord is good.
You are drawing near to him, the living stone whom human beings rejected, but who is chosen and honored in God's sight.
You too, like living stones, be built up and become spiritual temples and holy priests, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable before God through Jesus Christ.
For it is said in Scripture: “Look, I am laying in Zion a chosen and precious stone as the cornerstone, and whoever believes in it will not be put to shame.”
This honor, therefore, has been given to you who believe. But for those who do not obey,
he is a stone of stumbling and a rock that causes people to fall. They stumble over him because they do not obey the word; to this they were appointed.

But you are a chosen race serving as priests for the kingdom, a holy nation, a redeemed community, so that you may proclaim the praises of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
Once you were not considered a people, but now you are God's people. Nor had mercy been shown to you, but now mercy has been poured out upon you.
My dear friends, I ask you, as strangers and temporary residents, to keep away from all the desires of the body, which wage war against the soul.
Let your conduct be good before all people, so that those who speak evil of you may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day of examination.
Submit to all people for God's sake: to kings because of their authority,
and to judges because they are sent by him to punish wrongdoers and to praise those who do good.
For this is God's will: that by your good deeds you should silence foolish people who do not know God.
As free people, not as people who make their freedom a cover for their wickedness, but as servants of God.
Honor everyone. Love your brothers and sisters. Fear God. Honor kings.
Those among you who are slaves, submit to your masters with fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the harsh and difficult.
For those who, because of a good conscience, endure hardships that come upon them unjustly find favor before God.
But what praise is there for those who endure suffering because of their own wrongdoing? Yet when you do what is good and are afflicted and endure it, then your praise before God is great.
For to this you were called, because Christ also died for us and left us this example, so that you should walk in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth.
When he was insulted, he did not insult in return, and when he suffered, he did not threaten. Instead, he entrusted his case to the righteous judge.
He took all our sins and carried them in his body up to the cross, so that, having died to sin, we might live in his righteousness. For by his wounds you were healed.
For you were wandering like sheep, but now you have returned to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.
Likewise, you wives, submit to your husbands, so that you may win over those who do not obey the word, without effort, through your good conduct,
when they see that you conduct yourselves with reverence and purity.
Do not adorn yourselves with outward ornaments—with braided hair, gold jewelry, or fine clothes.
Instead, adorn yourselves in the hidden person of the heart, with a humble spirit that does not decay—an adornment precious in God's sight.
For this is how the holy women of long ago, who placed their hope in God, adorned themselves and submitted to their husbands.
Sarah, for example, submitted to Abraham and called him “my lord.” You become her daughters through good deeds, without being shaken by any fear.

Likewise, you husbands, live with your wives with understanding. Treat them with honor as fragile vessels, because they too inherit with you the gift of eternal life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.
Finally, all of you should live in harmony. Share the suffering of those who suffer, love one another, and be compassionate and humble.
Do not repay anyone evil for evil or insult for insult. Instead, give a blessing, for you were called to this, so that you might inherit a blessing.
Therefore, whoever desires life and loves to see good days must keep their tongue from evil and their lips from speaking deceit.
Let them turn away from evil and do good; let them seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears listen to them, but the face of the Lord is against the wicked.
And who will harm you if you are eager to do good?
But even if you suffer for righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear those who threaten you, and do not be troubled.
Instead, honor the Lord Christ as holy in your hearts. Be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for an explanation of the hope of your faith, with humility and reverence,
keeping a good conscience, so that those who speak against you as though you were evildoers may be ashamed as people who slander your good conduct in Christ.
For it is better for you to endure suffering while doing good, if that is God's will, rather than while doing evil.
For Christ also died once for our sins, the righteous one for sinners, to bring you near to God. He died in the body and came to life in the spirit.
And he preached to the souls who were held in Sheol.

These were the ones who had disobeyed long ago in the days of Noah, when God in his patience commanded an ark to be built in the hope of their repentance. Only eight souls entered it and survived through the water.
You too are saved in baptism, according to that pattern—not by washing dirt from your bodies, but by confessing God with a pure conscience, and through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
He was raised up to heaven and is at the right hand of God, and angels, authorities, and powers have been subjected to him.
If, then, Christ suffered for you in the flesh, arm yourselves with this same way of thinking. For everyone who dies in his body has ceased from all sins.
So that he may no longer live for human desires during his remaining time in the body, but for the will of God.
For the time that has passed is enough for you to have carried out the will of the pagans, in debauchery, drunkenness, indecency, singing, and the worship of demons.
And now they are astonished and speak abusively against you because you do not indulge with them in that former debauchery.
They will give an account to God, who is ready to judge the dead and the living.
For this reason the good news was proclaimed even to the dead, so that they might be judged in the flesh like human beings, but live in God in the spirit.
But the end of everything has arrived. Therefore be self-controlled and alert for prayer.
Above everything, have fervent love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to strangers without grumbling.
Each of you should use the gift he has received from God to serve his companions, as good stewards of God's varied grace.

Whoever speaks should speak as God's word. Whoever serves should do so with the strength that God gives him, so that in everything you do, God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and honor forever and ever. Amen.
My beloved, do not be astonished at the trials that happen to you, as though something strange were happening to you, because they happen to test you.
Instead, rejoice that you share in Christ's sufferings, so that you may also rejoice and be glad when his glory is revealed.
If you are insulted because of Christ's name, you are blessed, because the glorious Spirit of God rests upon you.
Only let none of you suffer as a murderer, a thief, or an evildoer.
But if someone suffers as a Christian, he should not be ashamed, but should glorify God in this name.
For it is time for judgment to begin with God's household. And if it begins with us, what will be the end of those who do not obey God's good news?
And if the righteous person is saved only with difficulty, where will the wicked person and the sinner be found?
Therefore, those who suffer according to God's will should entrust their souls to him as to a faithful Creator, while doing good deeds.
Now I appeal to the elders among you, as your fellow elder, a witness of Christ's sufferings, and a sharer in his glory that is to be revealed:
Shepherd the flock of God entrusted to you, and care for it spiritually—not under compulsion, but willingly; not for dishonest gain, but with all your heart.
Not as masters over the flock, but as a good example to them.
Then, when the chief shepherd is revealed, you will receive from him a crown of glory that does not fade.
And you young people, submit to your elders. Clothe yourselves firmly in humility toward one another, because God opposes those who exalt themselves but gives grace to the humble.
Therefore humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, so that it may lift you up at the proper time.
Throw all your worries onto God, because he cares for you.
Be alert and be mindful, because your enemy Satan roars and prowls like a lion, seeking someone to devour.
Therefore stand against him, remaining firm in faith. Know that these same sufferings are also afflicting your brothers and sisters in the world.

But the God of grace, who called us to his eternal glory through Jesus Christ, has granted us that, as we endure these small afflictions, we may be strengthened, made firm, and established in him forever.
To him belong glory, dominion, and honor forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother, I have written these few words to you. I urge you and testify that this is the true grace of God, in which you stand.
The chosen church in Babylon sends you greetings, as does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. Peace be with all who are in Christ. Amen.
